cards.explanation: The answer is the poor and the needy. Verse 1 says these women oppress the poor and crush the needy. Those are the people getting pressed down. Then they turn to their husbands and say, "Bring us more to drink." I think that tells you a lot about where their attention was.

The answer is that they will be taken away with hooks. The Lord GOD swears by His holiness that they will be taken away with hooks, and their posterity with fishhooks (Amos 4:2). Posterity means the ones who come after them. He swears it by His holiness, friends, so this isn't a small warning.

The answer is True. The LORD says, "You will go out through broken walls, each one straight ahead of her…" (Amos 4:3). So the walls are broken, and each woman goes straight ahead. After that, they are cast out toward Harmon.

The answer is that He tells them to transgress and rebel even more. "Go to Bethel and transgress; rebel even more at Gilgal!" Those are the LORD's words in verse 4, and I think they're startling to hear. He sets their rebellion right beside their sacrifices every morning and tithes every three days, so all that religious activity doesn't cancel out the transgressing. Verse 5 says this is what the children of Israel love to do, and then verse 6 says, "…yet you did not return to Me…"
The answer is False. The LORD tells them to offer leavened bread as a thank offering and to "…loudly proclaim your freewill offerings." So the instruction is to be loud, not quiet, friends.

The answer is that it's what they love to do. The LORD says it Himself: "For that is what you children of Israel love to do…" declares the Lord GOD. He gives that as the reason, and the text gives no other. Love is the word He uses.

The answer is that they did not return to Him. The LORD says, "…yet you did not return to Me…" declares the LORD. He brought lack of bread to all their towns, and the response He names is that they did not return. You'll be hearing that line again, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, "I sent rain on one city but withheld it from another." Then He says, "One field received rain; another without rain withered." So it differed from city to city and field to field.

The answer is False. The people staggered from city to city for water to drink, "…but they were not satisfied…" They kept searching, and it didn't satisfy them. The LORD then says again, "…yet you did not return to Me…"

The answer is True. The LORD says, "I struck you with blight and mildew in your growing gardens and vineyards; the locust devoured your fig and olive trees…" So the gardens and vineyards were hit, and the fig and olive trees were hit too. Then comes the line we keep hearing: "…yet you did not return to Me…"

The answer is Egypt. The LORD says, "I sent plagues among you like those of Egypt…" He picks Egypt as the comparison. It's a heavy verse, friends, and it ends with the same sad line: "…yet you did not return to Me…"

The answer is the stench of their camp. The LORD says, "I filled your nostrils with the stench of your camp…" This is a heavy verse, with the sword and the plagues in it. It still ends the same way: "…yet you did not return to Me…"

The answer is Sodom and Gomorrah. The LORD says, "Some of you I overthrew as I overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah…" He ties what happened to Israel to those two cities. Then He says they were like a firebrand snatched from a blaze, and still, "…yet you did not return to Me…"

The answer is to prepare to meet their God. The LORD says, "…prepare to meet your God, O Israel!" That's the command after everything He listed. It's the line the whole passage has been leading to, friends.
The answer is False. Verse 13 says that He "…reveals His thoughts to man…" He shows them to people instead of keeping them hidden. Same verse, same God who forms the mountains and creates the wind.
The answer is True. Verse 13 says He "…turns the dawn to darkness…" It sits right beside the mountains and the wind in that list. Then it finishes with His name: the LORD, the God of Hosts.
